item.title: PIAA GIRLS BASKETBALL: Six Lackawanna League teams ready for first round
item.description: Mountain View trailed Holy Cross by nine points with six minutes left in the third quarter of its District 2 Class 2A semifinal and rallied for a victory. In the final at Mohegan Arena at Casey Plaza, it was down 10 points to Wyoming Seminary, yet came back in the fourth quarter to win and claim its second straight Class 2A title and fourth consecutive district crown. item.title: COLLEGE FOOTBALL: Holtz found success when recruiting Northeast Pennsylvania
item.description: From Rocket Ismail to Ron Powlus. Add in Jake Kelchner and Tim Ruddy. Lou Holtz left a lasting impression on high school football across District 2. Holtz, the College Football Hall of Fame who won 249 games over 33 seasons at William & Mary, North Carolina State, Arkansas, Minnesota, South Carolina and, most notably, Notre Dame, died Wednesday in Orlando, Florida. item.title: PIAA BASKETBALL: Valley View returns to state playoffs with all new starting lineup
item.description: ARCHBALD — One year ago, the Valley View boys basketball team went on a roller-coaster ride filled with excitement and thrills, enjoying March Madness all the way to the PIAA Class 4A semifinals. The Cougars reveled in the historic season. Five starters — Beyon McLean, Noah Veno, Aidan Smola, Nick Kucharski and Tyler Scoblick — played together for the final time in a 64-44 loss to eventual champion Devon Prep at Parkland High School. item.title: AOH donation helps two families
item.description: The Ancient Order of Hibernians Paul “Hook” Division Four Man of the Year, retired Judge Tom Munley, presents two checks to the Rev.
